Definition: Whether government taxes, customs duties, and other revenue can be paid using the instant digital payment system, indicating integration of payment infrastructure with tax administration systems.
Comments: Liberia has active digital revenue collection via mobile tax payments and bank/online channels: USAID/DAI write-up states citizens can pay most taxes and many fees using mobile phones; it also notes up to 50% of the country's taxes are paid via commercial bank branches/online portals.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed with a more current primary source: LRA's July 2025 press release confirms its Integrated Orange Mobile Money Platform links directly to the Liberia Integrated Tax Administration System (LITAS), enabling tax and fee payment across 18 government ministries/agencies via Orange (*144#) and Lonestar MTN (*156#), corroborating the original DAI account. Score of 3 (Yes/comprehensive) retained.

Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: CBL has direct operational responsibilities for IIPS settlement: Participation Agreement states CBL will hold/manage settlement accounts (USD/LRD), process daily settlements, provide reports, support reconciliation, and move funds on the Switch Operator's instructions; IIPS is also "regulated and supervised by the Central Bank of Liberia." This indicates central bank direct operation of key functions (settlement and supervision).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Strongly confirmed: CBL's September 2025 NEPS-IIPS Directive and December 2025 Participation Agreement show CBL directly holds/manages USD and LRD settlement accounts, processes daily settlements and moves funds between providers, while ThitsaWorks operates the switch technology and CBL regulates/supervises the system overall — direct operational involvement beyond mere regulation. Score of 5 (Direct Operation) retained.

This supports at least annual public performance reporting rather than more frequent reporting.

revision_notes: Confirmed via the official CBL website: annual reports (2023, 2024 and 2025 editions located) contain detailed payment-system tables (mobile money subscribers/agents, systemically important payment system data, retail payment systems). Score of 3 (Annual) retained; source upgraded from a Scribd mirror to the official CBL PDF.

Definition: Whether payment system governance explicitly includes mechanisms to ensure inclusivity and represent interests of vulnerable populations, including provisions for input from all participant types, consumer representatives, small providers, or explicit financial inclusion mandates in governance documents.
Comments: Liberia's National Financial Inclusion Strategy (NFIS) 2020–2024 frames financial inclusion via digital channels as supporting poverty alleviation aligned with the Government's Pro-Poor Agenda for Prosperity and Development (PAPD), and states implementation will be guided by a multi-stakeholder steering committee (government agencies, development partners, private sector associations). This is evidence of partial pro-poor governance orientation, but not an explicit consumer/poor representation mandate in payment-system scheme governance.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed and updated: the 2020-2024 NFIS (multi-stakeholder steering committee, pro-poor framing) has now expired; a 2026 CBL-led assessment found it was weakest on consumer protection and financial literacy and often "measured the wrong things," and a successor National Financial Inclusion and Education Strategy (NFIES) 2026-2030 is still being drafted (workshops held April-May 2026), with no dedicated consumer/poor-representation governance body yet in place for the payment system specifically. Score of 2 (Partial) retained.

Definition: Percentage of the adult population (15+ years) who have made at least one digital payment transaction through the instant payment system in the past 90 days, indicating active usage rather than just account ownership.
Comments: World Bank Global Findex 2024 reported account ownership in Liberia at 52% by end-2024; given strong role of mobile wallets in this account ownership, this suggests active digital finance users likely in 50–69% range. (Note: account ownership is not identical to active usage, but is the closest quantified indicator found in reviewed evidence.)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: No Liberia-specific "90-day active digital payment user" figure was found. Global Findex (survey year 2024) puts account ownership at 52%, and CBL's own Governor stated in a 2025 speech that Liberia has "more than 3 million active mobile money subscribers" — a figure that, against an adult (15+) population of roughly 3 million, is implausibly high and likely double-counts multi-wallet holders, so it cannot be used as a percentage. Retaining code 3 (50-69%) on the Findex account-ownership proxy as the best available indicator, but flagging for human review given the mismatch with the CBL claim.

Definition: Whether independent external audits of payment system security, operations, financial controls, and compliance are conducted by third-party auditors, and whether audit results or summaries are made public.
Comments: CBL Annual Report 2024 notes the Bank undertook measures following the General Auditing Commission (GAC) compliance audit and other external audit reports, indicating existence of independent audits/reviews, but these audits are not necessarily published in full within the payment system context.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The official CBL 2024 Financial Statements, published openly on cbl.org.lr, carry a signed independent external auditor's opinion (IFRS-compliant) alongside references to a General Auditing Commission compliance audit — evidence of independent, and in a general institutional sense public, audit activity. However, these are institution-wide financial audits, not audits specifically scoped to IIPS/payment-system security, operations or compliance, so it is unclear whether they satisfy this variable's intent. Retaining code 2 (Private Audits) and flagging for human review to confirm whether the published institutional audit should count as "Public Audits" for this payment-system-specific variable.
